shell_login_subtitle: Quadeck manages services with root privileges. Please log in.
shell_setup_subtitle: Set the admin password. The install script shows the setup token; as root you can get it any time with “quadeck setup-token”.
shell_unlock_needSystem: Starting, stopping and other changes to the server need the password of an administrator (root or a member of wheel/sudo).
shell_unlock_needQuadeck: Starting, stopping and other changes to the server need the Quadeck password.
shell_unlock_afterwards: Actions then stay unlocked for {min} minutes.
shell_actions_stopHint: The service will no longer be reachable afterwards.
shell_jobs_background: Keeps running in the background, even if this window is closed.
shell_install_ostree: rpm-ostree: the package only becomes active after a reboot.
overview_subtitle: {host} · live via Podman socket and D-Bus
overview_edit_help: Edit mode: drag cards by the handle, resize them at the bottom right corner. Tiles can be moved and resized the same way; clicking a tile opens name, icon, group and URL.
overview_alert_stateFailed: The unit is in state failed.
overview_storage_tempSmart: From SMART, read every 30 minutes: the kernel has no sensor for this disk (for SATA, load the drivetemp module)
overview_services_detected: discovered automatically from Caddy and Quadlets, plus your own links
overview_services_empty: No services yet. Quadeck reads the routes from Caddy (admin API or /etc/caddy/Caddyfile); you can add your own links above.
overview_services_removeBody: The manually created link will be deleted.
overview_metrics_retention: Saved every 30 s, kept for 7 days. Gaps: Quadeck was not running at the time.
overview_metrics_intelNote: Intel iGPUs report no utilization without root privileges – shown is the current clock relative to the maximum clock, which rises under load (e.g. transcoding).
overview_chart_empty: No data in this time range yet.
overview_dialog_iconsOffline: Icon collection not available offline – enter the slug directly (e.g. “home-assistant”).
units_subtitle: Containers, Quadlets and system units – controlled via systemd
timers_list_intro: Schedules run as systemd timers – the successor of cron. Missed runs are caught up, the output goes to the journal.
timers_editor_descriptionPlaceholder: Copy photos to the backup disk
timers_editor_persistent: Catch up on missed runs (server was off)
timers_editor_deleteBody: Timer and service are stopped and both unit files are removed.
timers_schedule_vendor: The timer comes from a package – its file stays untouched.
timers_schedule_dropInBefore: Quadeck stores the new schedule as the drop-in
timers_schedule_modified: (The files were changed by hand, so only the schedule can be adjusted here.)
quadlets_list_empty: No Quadlets yet. Use “New” or “Compose import”.
quadlets_list_pick: Select a file on the left.
quadlets_compose_startUnits: Start the units after creating them
quadlets_editor_otherEntries: Other entries stay unchanged (edit them in the text view):
quadlets_editor_saveNote: Saved via the root helper, followed by systemctl daemon-reload. The previous version stays in the history.
quadlets_editor_deleteBody: {unit} will be stopped and the file deleted. It is kept in the history.
quadlets_remove_imageShared: Image {name} stays: another Quadlet uses it too.
quadlets_remove_volumesWarn: The data in these volumes is gone afterwards. This cannot be undone.
quadlets_remove_volumeShared: Volume {name} stays: another Quadlet uses it too.
quadlets_remove_binds: Folders on the host are always kept:
quadlets_history_diffNote: Difference between this version and the current state in the editor:
quadlets_history_load: Load this version into the editor
systemd_empty_subtitle: Select a unit in the list and choose “Edit”
systemd_unit_quadletMiddle: – changes to the container belong in the
systemd_unit_quadletAfter: ; overrides can be added here as well.
systemd_unit_timerBefore: Created by Quadeck as a schedule – easier to manage under
systemd_unit_timerAfter: . Once the files are changed by hand, the Timer page only edits them via drop-in.
systemd_unit_template: Instance of a template: the main file applies to all instances. An override here only affects this instance.
systemd_unit_overridesNote: Overrides (drop-ins in {dir}) replace single settings of the main file – package updates leave them alone. Later files win.
systemd_form_otherEntries: Other entries stay unchanged (edit them in the text view):
systemd_editor_vendorNote: This file belongs to a package – changes to it would be lost with the next update. Change settings with an override.
systemd_editor_dropinBody: will be deleted; the remaining files apply again. A running service only picks this up at its next restart.
systemd_editor_fragmentBefore: {unit} will be stopped and disabled, and
systemd_editor_keptInHistory: The content stays in the history.
systemd_create_subtitle: Own unit in {dir} – for schedules use Units → Timers
systemd_create_invalidName: Letters, digits, - _ . and a suffix like .service
podman_fields_unqualifiedsearchregistrie: Where “nginx” without a registry is looked up, e.g. docker.io, quay.io (comma-separated).
podman_fields_shortnamemode_help: enforcing: abort on multiple matches instead of guessing.
podman_fields_logdriver_help: journald: container logs in the journal (recommended).
podman_fields_tz_help: “local” uses the time zone of the host.
podman_config_missing: not present yet – Podman uses the defaults from /usr/share/containers
podman_config_saveNote: Checked as TOML before writing. Applies to newly started containers.
podman_updates_introMiddle: pulls new images for containers with
podman_updates_noTimer: podman-auto-update.timer is not present on this system.
podman_all_on: AutoUpdate=registry now applies to all containers
podman_all_noteAfter: (Podman 5). Applies to all containers after daemon-reload and overrides AutoUpdate= in individual files. Images must be fully qualified (docker.io/…).
podman_all_unsupported: Needs Podman 5 or newer (installed: {version}). Until then, set AutoUpdate=registry per file.
disks_page_subtitleMounts: Mounting via /etc/fstab – checked before anything is written
disks_page_subtitleSmart: SMART health of all drives – history, self-tests, what to do
disks_smart_readAt: Read {when} · automatically every 30 minutes, sleeping drives are not woken up
disks_smart_notInstalled: smartctl is not installed – without the smartmontools package Quadeck cannot read the SMART values of the drives.
disks_temp_noModule: The temperature of {disks} only comes from SMART every 30 minutes: the kernel module drivetemp is not loaded. For live values from the kernel:
disks_temp_noSensor: {disks} reports no temperature to the kernel although drivetemp is loaded (typical for USB enclosures and RAID controllers). The value therefore comes from SMART every 30 minutes.
disks_smart_historyKept: History values are stored hourly and kept for one year.
disks_card_shortStarted: Short self-test started on {name} (about 2 minutes; the drive stays usable)
disks_card_longStarted: Long self-test started on {name} (several hours; the drive stays usable)
disks_card_standbyText: The drive is asleep – it is not woken up for SMART. Values on the next read while it is active.
disks_card_unsupportedText: {msg} – normal for virtual drives; for USB enclosures one with SAT support often helps.
disks_detail_noHistory: No history yet – values are stored hourly.
disks_detail_errorCountersTitle: Error counters – rising values are the warning sign
disks_mounts_introBefore: Which disks are mounted where at boot ({path}). Every change is checked first – device, file system, driver,
disks_mounts_introAfter: , systemd's fstab generator and a test mount with the chosen options. System entries are left untouched.
disks_mounts_noEntries: No data disks in the fstab yet.
disks_mounts_allIncluded: All file systems are in the fstab.
disks_mounts_mountedNotInFstab: · currently mounted at {at}, but not in the fstab – gone after a reboot
disks_mounts_blocksBootTitle: If the disk is missing at boot, the server stops in emergency mode. “nofail” prevents that.
disks_mounts_uuidHelp: With the UUID the entry stays correct even if sdb becomes sdc after a rebuild.
disks_mounts_nofailHelp: If it is missing or broken, the server boots anyway.
disks_mounts_nofailWarn: Without nofail the server stops in emergency mode at boot if the disk is missing.
disks_mounts_automountHelp: The boot does not wait for the disk; it is mounted when first opened.
disks_mounts_harden: Harden as a pure data disk (nodev, nosuid)
disks_mounts_hardenHelp: Device files and setuid programs on the disk are ignored.
disks_mounts_roHelp: Nothing on the disk can be changed.
disks_mounts_compressHelp: New files are compressed transparently – saves space, costs some CPU.
disks_mounts_fatHelp: {fs} has no Linux permissions – owner and permissions apply to all files:
disks_mounts_wouldBlock: This entry would block the boot if the disk is missing – you have to confirm that explicitly when saving.
disks_mounts_checked: Checked – a test mount follows when saving.
disks_mounts_installPackage: Install the package: System → Installed, or
disks_mounts_rollback: If a step fails after writing, Quadeck restores the previous fstab.
disks_mounts_confirmCritical: {targets} has no “nofail”: if the disk is missing at boot, the server stops in emergency mode and is only reachable again after intervention at the console. I want it this way anyway.
files_page_subtitle: Files in the data areas – copy, move, rename, delete
files_explorer_noRoots: No data areas found (/mnt, /srv, /media, /home, /data). Add your own with QUADECK_FILE_ROOTS.
files_editor_crlf: Windows line endings (CRLF) – kept when saving
files_editor_binary: This is not a text file – Quadeck does not open it in the editor.
files_editor_tooLarge: Larger than 2 MB – too large for the editor.
files_editor_confirmText: Quadeck writes the file anew; owner and permissions stay the same.
files_explorer_deleteBody: Folders are deleted with all their content. There is no trash.
shares_page_subtitle: SMB (Windows, macOS, Android) and NFS (Linux) – create, change, control services
shares_smbDialog_usersPlaceholder: empty = all Samba users, e.g. tristan @family
shares_smbDialog_passwordHint: Samba users need their own password:
shares_nfsDialog_syncTitle: sync: confirm only once on disk (safer)

match.hasAur=true: Packages via {manager} · AUR via {aur} · container images via podman auto-update
match.hasAur=*: Packages via {manager} · container images via podman auto-update

system_updates_readFirst: read before updating – sometimes manual steps are needed
system_updates_noHelper: yay or paru is not installed – updates are shown but not installed.
system_updates_noAurUser: No user found for the AUR helper – set QUADECK_AUR_USER.
system_updates_buildsAs: Builds as {user} with {helper}; pacman runs via sudo (without a password only for the duration of the job).
system_updates_imagesHint: “Update all” uses podman auto-update with rollback: if a container does not start with the new image, the old one is restored. Individually: pull the new image and restart the unit.
system_updates_unreadNews: There is unread Arch news – please read it first.

match.nPlural=one: {helper} builds {n} package as {user}. PKGBUILDs are not shown – only update packages you trust.
match.nPlural=other: {helper} builds {n} packages as {user}. PKGBUILDs are not shown – only update packages you trust.

system_updates_imagesBody: {names} are restarted with the new image (podman auto-update, with rollback).
system_packages_protectedHint: Protected system package – cannot be removed here.

match.nPlural=one: {n} package will be removed – the selected ones and dependencies nothing else needs:
match.nPlural=other: {n} packages will be removed – the selected ones and dependencies nothing else needs:

system_packages_blocked: Protected packages would be affected ({names}) – removal is blocked.
system_config_intro: An update brought a new version but did not overwrite your changed one.
system_config_hint: Compare, then keep yours, take over the new one or merge both. On the console the same works with {cmd}.
system_config_binary: Not a text file or too big – only delete or keep here.
system_config_diffIntro: Difference from your version ({minus}) to the new one from the package ({plus}):
system_config_noLive: {live} does not exist – the new version:
system_config_mergeIntro: Your version to edit – take over what you need from the new one (see the difference above). Exactly this text is saved.
system_config_mkinitcpio: Then the initramfs is rebuilt (mkinitcpio -P) – as a job with output.
boot_reloadsWhenBack: The page reloads as soon as it is reachable again. That usually takes one to two minutes.

match.hasEntry=true: Containers and services are shut down cleanly and start again afterwards with “{entry}”.
match.hasEntry=*: Containers and services are shut down cleanly and start again afterwards.

boot_jobRunning: “{title}” is running right now – better wait.
boot_grub: GRUB – Quadeck only shows the kernel parameters here; GRUB manages entries and the default itself.
boot_kernelHint: Several kernel variants can be installed side by side; use “Boot this once” to switch back and forth.
boot_dkmsHint: DKMS modules (e.g. NVIDIA, ZFS) are built for every kernel with the matching headers.
boot_paramsSd: in the {options} line of the entry under {dir} or in {cmdline}
boot_newFileText: – a copy of the default entry with the same parameters, only kernel and initramfs swapped. Existing entries stay unchanged.
boot_removeKernelBody: Removes the package {pkg} (and the headers, if installed) with pacman. The boot entry then points nowhere and can be removed here.
boot_startsOnceAfter: . The reboot after that uses the default again – if something goes wrong, a reset is enough.
boot_firmwareStays: The server stays in the firmware menu until someone on site continues – it is not reachable over the network then.
boot_allStopped: All containers and services are stopped. The server is unreachable for one to two minutes, Quadeck included.
boot_jobAborted: “{title}” is still running and would be aborted.
boot_editor_fileHint: in {dir} – the name is also the id for bootctl
boot_editor_lockedNote: {id} is the default or the running entry and stays as it is. This becomes a copy: save it, boot it once and, if everything works, make it the default.
boot_editor_confirmText: Takes effect the next time this entry boots. Every version stays in the history.
boot_editor_testText: Before an entry becomes the default, boot it once. If something goes wrong, a reset is enough – the old default boots after that.
boot_editor_loaded: Version from {date} loaded – not saved yet
boot_editor_renameHint: If the entry is the default or set for the next boot, Quadeck moves that to the new name with bootctl.
boot_form_titleHelp: The name of the entry in the boot menu.
boot_form_kernelHelp: The kernel image on the boot partition (the linux line). When you switch, Quadeck swaps the matching initramfs too.
boot_form_initrdHelp: Loaded before the kernel (the initrd lines). Microcode has to come first – Quadeck puts it in front.
boot_form_microcode: Microcode update for the CPU – fixes processor bugs, should always be there
boot_form_initramfs: Initramfs: drivers and scripts the kernel needs to find the system
boot_form_fallback: Fallback initramfs with all drivers – larger, for emergencies
boot_form_otherInitrd: Another file loaded before the kernel
boot_form_paramsHelp: The options line – handed to the kernel at boot. A wrong parameter can stop the boot, so boot it once first.
boot_form_paramUnknown: Not a parameter Quadeck can explain
boot_form_otherLines: Other lines ({keys}) stay as they are – editable as text.
boot_editor_deleteBody: Deletes {path}. Quadeck keeps the contents in the history; create an entry with this name again to load them from there.
hardware_copyHttps: Copying only works over https or localhost – please select the text
hardware_vmUnavailable: not available or turned off in the BIOS
hardware_slotsUnreadable: Slots not readable (dmidecode missing or virtual machine).
hardware_eccYes: yes – memory errors are detected and corrected
hardware_gpuHint: With this line in the [Container] section of the Quadlet, Jellyfin or Immich, for example, use the GPU for hardware transcoding.
hardware_usbHint: The path under /dev/serial/by-id stays the same even when ttyUSB0 becomes ttyUSB1 after a reboot – enter it like this in Home Assistant or Zigbee2MQTT (AddDevice= in the Quadlet).
hardware_noSensors: No sensors readable (normal in VMs; otherwise the kernel module is often missing, e.g. nct6775 or it87).
network_subtitle: Interfaces, routes, DNS, open ports, firewall, reverse proxy and speed test
network_fw_blocked_title: The firewall does not let connections from outside through
network_fw_podman_title: Podman opens published container ports itself
network_firewall_noFirewall: No firewall active: everything listening on “all interfaces” is reachable in the local network. Behind a router this is common at home – from outside only what the router forwards gets through.
network_firewall_blocked: , but blocked: {ports}. Intended? Otherwise allow it in the firewall (e.g.
proxy_intro: Domains that Caddy forwards to containers and services. Nothing is saved before Caddy has checked it; then Caddy loads the new config without interruption.
proxy_status_api: Caddy is running – changes via the admin API
proxy_status_container: Caddy is running in the container {c}
proxy_table_also: Also in the Caddyfile: {parts} – editable as text only.
proxy_table_unstructured: The Caddyfile is not organised in blocks (e.g. a single site without braces) – editable as text only.
proxy_pick_hint: Absolute path on the server, e.g. /home/tristan/docker/caddy/Caddyfile. Quadeck remembers it; QUADECK_CADDYFILE takes precedence.
proxy_pick_envHint: The path comes from QUADECK_CADDYFILE (/etc/quadeck/quadeck.env) and can only be changed there.
proxy_site_domainsHint: Separate several with commas. Caddy gets the HTTPS certificate itself – the domain must point to this server.
proxy_site_targetHint: Address where Caddy reaches the service, e.g. localhost:8096. Suggestions: containers with a published port.
proxy_site_lanOnly: Only reachable from the home network
proxy_site_lanOnlyHelp: Requests from the internet get 403 – only private addresses (LAN, VPN) get through.
proxy_site_authHelp: The browser asks for user and password before the page loads. Caddy only stores the hash.
proxy_site_authKeep: leave empty to keep the current password
proxy_site_compressHelp: Compress responses with zstd or gzip – faster over slow connections.
proxy_site_insecureTls: Target uses HTTPS with its own certificate
proxy_site_insecureTlsHelp: For devices like Proxmox or UniFi that only speak HTTPS with a self-signed certificate (target with https://).
proxy_site_tlsInternalHelp: For names that do not exist on the internet (e.g. .lan, .home.arpa): Caddy issues the certificate itself. Browsers warn until Caddy's root certificate is installed.
proxy_site_extraHelp: Everything else in this block, as written in the Caddyfile.
proxy_block_hint: Only this entry – the rest of the Caddyfile stays as it is.
proxy_text_revision: Version from {date} – save to restore it
proxy_confirm_steps: Caddy checks the new version, then {path} is saved (the previous one goes to the history) and Caddy is reloaded. If Caddy rejects it, everything stays as it is.
proxy_confirm_stopped: Caddy is not running: the file is saved and read at the next start.
proxy_done_api: Saved – Caddy loaded the new config
proxy_done_container: Saved – Caddy reloaded in the container
proxy_done_automatic: The Caddyfile is found automatically again
proxy_errors_badAddress: “{address}” is not a valid address (e.g. app.example.com or :8080)
proxy_errors_badTarget: “{u}” is not a valid target (e.g. localhost:8096 or jellyfin:8096)
proxy_errors_custom: {address} has its own settings – please edit it as text
proxy_errors_fileName: The file name must contain “Caddyfile” (e.g. Caddyfile or sites.caddyfile)
proxy_errors_envMissing: QUADECK_CADDYFILE points to {path}, there is no file
proxy_errors_json: {quadlet} starts Caddy with a JSON config – Quadeck cannot edit that
proxy_errors_notMounted: {quadlet} does not mount {containerPath} from the host – the file is inside the image, changes would be gone with the next start. To edit it, add to the Quadlet: Volume=/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:{containerPath}
proxy_errors_mountedMissing: {quadlet} mounts {path}, but there is no file
proxy_errors_notFound: No Caddyfile found – no Caddy Quadlet with a mounted Caddyfile, no caddy.service and no /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.
proxy_errors_notText: {path} is not a text file or too big
proxy_errors_unchecked: Not checked: Caddy is not running and cannot be started here – the file will be read the next time Caddy starts.
proxy_errors_changed: The Caddyfile was changed in the meantime – please reload and make the change again.
proxy_errors_rejected: Caddy rejects the file – nothing changed:
proxy_errors_reloadFailed: Reload failed – the old file is restored, Caddy keeps running unchanged:
proxy_errors_stopped: Saved. Caddy is not running – the change applies from the next start.
proxy_errors_authPassword: The password for the password protection is missing
proxy_errors_authShort: The password needs at least 8 characters
proxy_errors_braces: The curly braces in the other lines do not match
proxy_errors_oneBlock: Exactly one entry: domain(s), then a block with its lines
ssh_subtitle: Access to the server: keys, hardening, logins
ssh_install_what: No SSH server installed – without it the server can only be reached directly with screen and keyboard.
ssh_access_enabled: SSH now also starts at boot
ssh_access_fingerprints: Fingerprints of this server – compare them when connecting for the first time
ssh_hardening_passwordOnHelp: Bots keep trying passwords. Turn it off as soon as your key works.
ssh_hardening_passwordOffHelp: Good: login only with an added key.
ssh_hardening_rootYesHelp: Risky: root with password. Better log in as a normal user and use sudo.
ssh_hardening_rootOtherHelp: root cannot get in with a password.
ssh_hardening_allowedHelp: Optional: only these accounts may log in via SSH.
ssh_hardening_noKeys: No user has a key yet – add one first.
ssh_hardening_noInclude: sshd_config does not include sshd_config.d/*.conf – settings can only be applied here after adding “Include /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf”.
ssh_logins_none: No logins in the last 30 days (or no access to the journal).
ssh_logins_failedHint: As long as password login is on, these attempts have a chance – turn it off or set up fail2ban.
ssh_newDevice_step1: Create a key on the new device (once):
ssh_newDevice_step2Password: as long as password login is on, this works directly:
ssh_newDevice_step2Key: Paste the content of ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub above under “Keys” (password login is off, so ssh-copy-id does not work).
ssh_newDevice_step3: Connect and, the first time, compare the fingerprint with “Access” above:
ssh_keys_none: No key yet – {name} can only log in with a password.
ssh_preview_force: I can reach the server another way (screen/keyboard, IPMI) and want this anyway.
users_subtitle: Accounts on the server – login, password, groups, SSH keys, Samba
users_detail_adminHelp: May use sudo and unlock Quadeck.
users_login_noPassword: no password – login only with an SSH key
users_login_nothing: Neither password nor key – nobody can log in with this account.
users_login_sambaNone: no Samba password yet – shares can only be accessed as guest
users_password_sambaHelp: Only applies to access to shares (SMB) and is independent of the login password.
users_password_mismatch: The two entries do not match
users_create_mismatch: The two passwords do not match

match.admin=true: The account gets no password. You add the public key afterwards in the details – as administrator it still needs a password for sudo and to unlock Quadeck.
match.admin=*: The account gets no password. You add the public key afterwards in the details.

notifications_subtitle: The server lets you know when something is wrong – on your phone or in the chat
notifications_channels_none: No channel yet – without a channel nothing is sent. Easiest: install the ntfy app, make up a topic, enter it here.
notifications_channels_removeBody: Nothing will be sent to this channel anymore.

match.recovery=true: Each problem is reported once; when it is resolved, an all-clear follows.
match.recovery=*: Each problem is reported once; when it is resolved, no further message follows.

notifications_rules_speedRelativeAfter: % of the usual (average of the last 7 days)
notifications_rules_recovery: Send an all-clear when a problem is resolved
notifications_security_none: none (only a relay in your own network)
notifications_email_fromHelp: Most providers require your own address here.
notifications_dialog_topicHelp: On ntfy.sh anyone who knows the name can subscribe to a topic – so pick a name that is hard to guess.
timers_label_weekdays: Sun Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri Sat
format_date_months: Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec
api_lang_invalid: lang must be de or en
api_notifications_testBody: Notifications from Quadeck are getting through.
auth_error_passwordTooShort: Password must have at least {minLength} characters
auth_error_tooManyAttempts: Too many failed attempts. Please wait {seconds} s.
auth_error_tooManyParallel: Too many simultaneous login attempts. Please try again shortly.
boot_error_entriesBySystem: Boot entries are created by the system itself here (kernel-install/UKI) – or it is not systemd-boot
boot_error_noTemplateEntry: No readable default entry to use as a template
boot_error_imageMissing: {boot}{file} is missing – wait for the installation first (mkinitcpio creates the initramfs)
boot_error_entryInUse: The default entry and the running entry stay
boot_error_noSystemdBoot: No systemd-boot – Quadeck only changes systemd-boot here
boot_error_entryLocked: Quadeck does not change the default or the running entry in place: make a copy, boot it once, then make it the default
boot_error_changedMeanwhile: The file was changed in the meantime – open it again
boot_error_invalidFileName: File name: letters, digits, @ _ . + ~ -, ending in .conf
boot_error_entryIsOneshot: The entry is set for the next boot – undo that first
boot_error_lastEntry: This is the last entry that boots
boot_check_tooLarge: Too large for a boot entry
boot_check_unknownKey: systemd-boot does not know {key} – a typo?
boot_check_relativePath: {file}: paths start with / (from the boot partition)
boot_check_fileMissing: {file} does not exist on the boot partition
boot_check_noKernel: No kernel: a linux line (or efi/uki) is missing
boot_check_noRoot: options lacks root= – without it the kernel does not find the system
boot_check_noTitle: No title – the menu shows the file name instead
files_error_sensitive: Quadeck shows keys and credentials only after unlocking
files_error_tooLarge: Too large for the editor (more than 2 MB)
files_error_changedMeanwhile: The file was changed in the meantime – open it again
files_error_demoNoContent: In the demo this is only a name without content
fstab_warn_networkUnchecked: Network drive – Quadeck does not check the source or whether it is reachable
fstab_warn_sourceNotDrive: Source {spec} is not a drive – only the entry itself is checked
fstab_warn_mountedElsewhere: {path} is already mounted at {mountPoints} – that stays so until the next reboot
fstab_error_mountPointIsFile: {file} is a file, not a directory
fstab_warn_mountPointNotEmpty: {file} is not empty – its content is hidden while the disk is mounted
fstab_job_writeFile: Write {path} (previous version as {path}.quadeck-bak and in the history)
fstab_error_bootCritical: {mountPoints} would block the boot if the disk is missing – set “nofail” or confirm explicitly
fstab_error_testMountFailed: Test mount failed – fstab stays unchanged:
fstab_error_busyOnRemove: {file} cannot be unmounted – it is in use (e.g. by a container, a share or an open shell)
fstab_error_restoredSuffix: – the previous fstab has been restored
fstab_error_remountFailed: Remounting with the new options failed:
fstab_error_systemNoMount: – is not mounted or unmounted here
fstab_error_busyOnUnmount: {target} cannot be unmounted – it is in use
links_error_httpOnly: Only http:// and https:// are allowed
links_error_iconSlug: Icon: only a slug from dashboard-icons, e.g. "home-assistant"
mail_error_loginRejected: Login rejected ({response}) – check user and password; many providers need an app password
mail_error_connectionRefused: Connection refused – check server and port
mail_error_noConnection: No connection to the SMTP server ({message}) – check port, encryption or firewall
mail_error_serverNotFound: SMTP server not found – check the name
mail_error_tlsMismatch: TLS mismatch – choose “SSL/TLS” for port 465, “STARTTLS” for 587
network_note_appProfiles: App profiles (e.g. OpenSSH) cannot be resolved to ports here.
network_note_customNftables: Custom nftables rules: Quadeck cannot reliably tell which ports are open.
notify_error_urlScheme: URL must start with http:// or https://
services_error_iconSlug: Icon: a slug from dashboard-icons, e.g. "home-assistant"
packages_error_aurAsRoot: AUR helpers do not run as root – set QUADECK_AUR_USER to a normal user
packages_error_sudoMissing: {helper} needs sudo to call pacman – sudo is not installed
packages_note_aurUpdateAs: AUR update with {helper} as {user} (pacman via sudo without a password only during this job)
configfiles_error_notListed: {path} is not (or no longer) in the list
configfiles_error_notConfigFile: Not a config file of a package
configfiles_error_saveOnlyDelete: Saved versions are only deleted – to take one over, edit the content and save it by hand
configfiles_error_binaryFile: Not a text file – only keep or delete here
configfiles_error_symlink: {path} is a symlink and is not overwritten
packages_error_noAurHelper: Neither yay nor paru is installed
packages_error_noAurUser: No user for AUR updates (set QUADECK_AUR_USER)
packages_error_kernelArchOnly: Kernel variants are only available on Arch (pacman) here
packages_error_jobNeedsRoot: quadeck job must run as root
packages_error_jobBusy: A job is already running – please wait until it is done
packages_job_runningAsUnit: (running as {unit}; output also in the journal)
packages_error_noManager: No supported package manager found (pacman, apt, dnf, zypper, apk, rpm-ostree)
packages_configHint_generic: The new package versions of the files lie next to them; compare and take over (e.g. with diff).
packages_configHint_rpmconf: New package versions lie next to them as .rpmnew; compare and take over (e.g. rpmconf -a).
packages_configHint_rpmnew: New package versions lie next to them as .rpmnew; compare and take over.
packages_configHint_apkNew: New versions lie next to them as .apk-new; compare and take over.
packages_configHint_ostree: On ostree, /etc is merged during the upgrade; check .rpmnew files by hand.
packages_error_ostreeNoRemove: On rpm-ostree systems packages are not removed one by one (rpm-ostree uninstall only for layered packages).
packages_error_ostreeRemove: Removing is not supported on rpm-ostree
packages_reboot_deploymentStaged: New deployment ready – a reboot activates it
helper_error_tooManyAttempts: Too many failed attempts. Please wait {seconds} s.
helper_error_notAdmin: {user} is not an administrator (root or group wheel/sudo)
helper_error_noPassword: {user} has no password set – use another account
helper_error_cryptUnavailable: Cannot verify the password hash (crypt(3) not available)
helper_error_invalidUnitAction: action must be start, stop or restart
helper_error_invalidShareKind: kind must be smb or nfs
helper_error_podmanSocketMissing: Podman socket {socket} missing – systemctl enable --now podman.socket
quadlets_lint_refMissing: {ref} does not exist (yet) – the unit will not start without it
quadlets_lint_generatorMissing: Quadlet generator not found – own checks only
quadlets_compose_portNotPublished: Port {port} without a host port is not published (expose only)
quadlets_compose_noServices: No services: found – is this a docker-compose.yml?
quadlets_compose_externalNetwork: Network {network} is external – it must already exist
quadlets_compose_externalVolume: Volume {volume} is external – it must already exist
quadlets_compose_buildNotConverted: build: is not converted – build the image first or create a .build file
quadlets_compose_relativePath: relative path {path} – change it to an absolute path
quadlets_compose_relativeEnvFile: env_file {path} is relative – enter an absolute path
quadlets_compose_privileged: privileged: true converted – check whether it is needed
shares_error_pathNotDir: {path} does not exist or is not a directory
shares_warn_guestWrite: Guests may write – anyone on the network can change or delete files
shares_warn_worldWritable: Write access for all hosts (*) – better restrict it to your own network
shares_warn_noRootSquash: no_root_squash: root on the client is root here too
smart_error_selfTestUnavailable: {disk} cannot run a self-test right now
ssh_warn_rootPassword: root may log in with a password – better “key only” or “no”
ssh_warn_passwordLogin: Password login is on – attackers can try out passwords
ssh_blocked_noWorkingKey: Without password login nobody could log in anymore: no allowed user has a working key.
ssh_blocked_noAllowedUser: No allowed user would be able to log in.
ssh_warn_stayLoggedIn: Stay logged in to your current SSH session and test access in a second one before closing it.
ssh_problem_writableByOthers: {what} is writable by others – sshd ignores the keys
ssh_error_noLoginAccount: User {user} cannot log in via SSH (no login account)
ssh_blocked_lastKey: This is the last working key and password login is off – afterwards nobody could get onto the server via SSH.
ssh_error_noService: No SSH service installed (package openssh or openssh-server)
ssh_keyError_unknownType: No known key type (expected e.g. “ssh-ed25519 AAAA… name@device”)
ssh_keyError_notBase64: Key data missing or not Base64
ssh_keyError_typeMismatch: Key data does not match the type {type}
ssh_weak_dsa: DSA is no longer accepted by current OpenSSH
ssh_weak_rsaShort: RSA with {bits} bits – too short today, better ed25519
ssh_keyError_hasOptions: Please add keys with options (from=, command= …) by hand
systemd_error_protectedUnit: {unit} belongs to Quadeck itself and is not changed here
systemd_verify_templateSkipped: systemd only checks template units as an instance – syntax checked only
systemd_readonly_protected: Belongs to Quadeck itself – changes here could lock Quadeck out
systemd_readonly_transient: Transient unit (systemd-run) – disappears when it ends
systemd_error_outsideDir: {path} is not in {dir} – change package files with an override
systemd_error_symlink: {path} is a symlink and will not be overwritten
systemd_warn_restartFailed: Saved, but {unit} does not restart: {reason} – see the journal
systemd_error_invalidName: Name: letters, digits, - _ . and a suffix like .service
systemd_warn_startFailed: Created, but the start failed: {reason} – see the journal
systemd_error_outsideUnitDir: {path} is not in {dir} – change package files with an override
timers_error_invalidAction: Action must be run, enable or disable
timers_error_unitExists: {unit} already exists – please choose another name
timers_error_notDeletable: {name} was not created by Quadeck and is not deleted here
timers_error_timerExists: {name}.timer already exists – please choose another name
users_note_rootProtected: root is the system account and is not deleted
users_error_inUse: The account is logged in or processes are running under it – log out or stop them first
users_error_nameExists: The name already exists (maybe as a group)
boot_timeout_menuHidden: Hide the menu (press a key at boot to see it)
boot_timeout_menuForce: Always wait until someone picks one
boot_warn_kernelNoEntry: {pkg} is installed but has no boot entry – “Create boot entry”
boot_warn_espTooSmall: Only {free} left on {path} – a kernel with initramfs needs {needed}. The next kernel update can fail and leave the server unbootable: remove old kernels or fallback images.
boot_warn_loaderOutdated: systemd-boot on the ESP ({espVersion}) is older than the installed systemd ({packageVersion}) – “Update boot loader” (bootctl update).
boot_warn_noDefaultEntry: No default entry found – systemd-boot then takes the first one in the list.
boot_param_rootflags: Options for mounting / (e.g. the btrfs subvolume)
boot_param_rw: Mount the system writable right away
boot_param_ro: Mount the system read-only first (fsck checks it before)
boot_param_cryptdevice: Encrypted partition that is unlocked at boot
boot_param_initrd: initramfs loaded along with the kernel
boot_param_loglevel: Only show kernel messages up to level {level}
boot_param_nowatchdog: Hardware watchdog off – a bit faster, but no automatic restart on hangs
boot_param_mitigationsOff: Protection against CPU vulnerabilities (Spectre & co.) turned off – faster, but less secure
boot_param_i915Guc: Intel GPU: load GuC/HuC – needed for hardware transcoding (QuickSync) in Jellyfin, Plex, Immich
boot_param_xeForceProbe: Intel GPU (Arc/Xe): force the new xe driver
boot_param_i915ForceProbe: Intel GPU: force the driver for cards not yet officially supported
boot_param_amdgpuFeatureMask: AMD GPU: power and overclocking features
boot_param_nvidiaModeset: NVIDIA: kernel mode setting (needed for Wayland and some containers)
boot_param_usbAutosuspendOff: USB power saving off – helps against USB disks that drop off
boot_param_usbAutosuspend: Suspend USB devices after this many idle seconds
boot_param_nvmeApstOff: NVMe power saving states off – helps against SSDs that vanish under load
boot_param_nvmeApst: NVMe: deepest allowed power saving state
boot_param_pcieAspmForce: Force PCIe power saving (even where the BIOS does not report it)
boot_param_pcieAspmPolicy: PCIe power saving level (powersupersave saves the most)
boot_param_intelIommuOn: IOMMU on – pass devices through to VMs (VFIO)
boot_param_amdIommu: AMD IOMMU – pass devices through to VMs
boot_param_vfioPciIds: Reserve these PCI devices for VMs
boot_param_consoleblank: Blank the console screen after {seconds} s
boot_param_console: Where kernel messages go (screen, serial port)
boot_param_zswapOn: Compressed cache in front of swap on
boot_param_unifiedCgroup: cgroups version (1 = v2 only, as Podman needs it)
boot_param_showStatus: Show the status of units at boot
boot_param_rdUdevLogLevel: Messages of udev in the initramfs
boot_param_rdShowStatus: Show the status of units in the initramfs
boot_param_hugepages: Reserve a fixed number of huge pages
boot_param_amdPstate: AMD CPU: frequency scaling via CPPC (active usually saves more)
boot_param_acpiOsi: Operating system reported to the BIOS (workaround for firmware bugs)
boot_param_acpiEnforceResources: ACPI resources (lax: sensors of some mainboards become readable)
boot_param_libataForce: Force settings for SATA ports (e.g. speed)
boot_param_randomTrustCpu: Trust the CPU’s random numbers at boot
boot_param_nomodeset: No graphics mode setting – only for troubleshooting, turns off hardware acceleration
boot_param_panic: Reboot {seconds} s after a kernel panic
boot_param_kvmIgnoreMsrs: KVM: ignore unknown CPU registers (Windows VMs)
boot_param_splitLockDetect: Split lock detection (off: some games, VMs faster)
boot_note_kernelRunning: Running right now – boot another kernel first
boot_note_kernelIsDefault: Is the default entry – make another kernel the default first
configfiles_hint_passwd: The new version does not know your users – taking it over would delete every account except root. Almost always: “Keep mine”.
configfiles_hint_shadow: Holds the passwords – never take over the package version.
configfiles_hint_group: The new version does not know your groups and memberships.
configfiles_hint_gshadow: Group passwords – never take over the package version.
configfiles_hint_shells: Lists the allowed shells; the new version does not know ones installed later (zsh, fish). Usually “Keep mine”.
configfiles_hint_fstab: Holds your disks – the package version would drop them from boot.
configfiles_hint_sudoers: A mistake here locks sudo – only change it by hand with visudo.
configfiles_hint_hosts: Holds your own names; the package version is empty.
configfiles_hint_sshd: Settings of the SSH server. Keep your changes (Port, password login, AllowUsers) – Quadeck’s own live in sshd_config.d/ and stay anyway. sshd -t checks the file before saving.
configfiles_hint_mkinitcpio: Builds the initramfs the kernel starts with. Be sure to keep your MODULES and HOOKS lines (encryption, btrfs, GPU, plymouth) – otherwise the server will not boot. Rebuild the initramfs afterwards.
configfiles_hint_mkinitcpioPreset: Preset for a kernel’s initramfs. Rebuild the initramfs afterwards.
configfiles_hint_pacman: Settings of pacman. Carry over your own changes: [multilib], ParallelDownloads, Color, IgnorePkg, your own repositories.
configfiles_hint_mirrorlist: List of download servers. If you did not maintain it yourself (or generate it with reflector), the new version can be taken over – but then uncomment at least one server.
configfiles_hint_localeGen: Which locales are generated. Keep your uncommented lines (e.g. de_DE.UTF-8), otherwise run locale-gen afterwards.
configfiles_hint_samba: Your shares are defined here – never simply take over the package version. testparm checks the file before saving.
configfiles_hint_systemd: Setting of a systemd service. The package version is usually all commented out; your own values are better placed in a drop-in (…conf.d/).
configfiles_hint_makepkg: Settings for building packages (AUR). Carry over your own values (MAKEFLAGS, COMPRESSZST), otherwise take the new version.
configfiles_hint_pam: Login rules (PAM). Careful: mistakes here can prevent logins. If you changed nothing, take over the new version.
configfiles_hint_containers: Settings of Podman. Keep your registries and storage locations.
configfiles_hint_grub: Settings for GRUB. Keep your GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX line; run grub-mkconfig afterwards.
configfiles_hint_tpm: Profiles for the TPM. Without changes of your own, the new version can be taken over.
configfiles_hint_orphanSave: Saved version of a removed package – not in use. If you need nothing from it, it can go.
configfiles_confirm_replace: {live} is replaced by the new version; your previous one is kept as {live}.quadeck-bak.
configfiles_confirm_keep: {path} is deleted; {live} stays as it is.
configfiles_confirm_merge: {live} is saved with your edited text (previous version as {live}.quadeck-bak), {path} is deleted.
configfiles_warn_mkinitcpioLines: Your {list} lines differ from the new version (e.g. sd-encrypt, btrfs, GPU modules). Taking it over could leave the server unbootable – please “Merge” and keep your lines.
configfiles_warn_sambaShares: The new version does not contain your shares ({list}) – taking it over would delete them. “Keep mine” or merge.
fstab_check_tooFewFields: Too few fields – at least source and mount point
fstab_check_tooManyFields: {count} fields – fstab has at most 6 (write spaces in paths as \040)
fstab_error_changedMeanwhile: The fstab has been changed in the meantime – please reload
fstab_check_mountPointNotAbsolute: The mount point must be an absolute path (/mnt/…)
fstab_check_pathNotNormalized: Give the path without “.”, “..”, double or trailing “/”
fstab_check_pathInvalidChars: Control characters and “#” are not allowed in the path
fstab_check_systemDir: {path} is a system directory – use e.g. /mnt/name or /srv/name
fstab_check_sourceInvalid: Source: give UUID=…, LABEL=…, PARTUUID=… or /dev/…
fstab_check_fsTypeInvalid: File system: e.g. ext4, xfs, btrfs
fstab_check_optionUnknown: Quadeck does not know option “{option}” for {vfstype} – the test mount shows whether the driver accepts it
fstab_check_roAndRw: ro and rw at the same time
fstab_check_noautoAutomount: noauto with automount: mounted on access only
fstab_check_passnoOneNotRoot: Check order 1 is meant for / – data disks 2 or 0
fstab_check_passnoNoFsck: {vfstype} is not checked with fsck at boot – set field 6 to 0
fstab_check_mountPointDuplicate: {file} is already in line {line} – a mount point may appear only once
fstab_check_noRootEntry: No entry for / – that is unusual
fstab_check_systemEntryChanged: A system entry would be changed or removed: {entries}
fstab_check_systemEntryAdded: A new system entry is not allowed: {entries}
hardware_status_linkWidthDown: runs at x{linkWidth} instead of x{maxLinkWidth}
hardware_warn_pcieDowngraded: {device} {link} – usually a slot that has fewer lanes or shares them with another one (see the mainboard manual).
hardware_warn_sataSlowLink: {disk}{model} is linked at {speed} instead of {limit} – often the cable or port; matches CRC errors in SMART.
hardware_warn_biosOld: The BIOS is from {year}. Newer versions often fix bugs and security holes – check the mainboard maker’s website.
hardware_note_virtualMachine: Runs in a virtual machine ({virt}) – slots, sensors and links then show the virtual hardware.
ini_lint_invalidLine: Line is neither a section, Key=Value nor a comment
ini_lint_duplicateKey: {key} is set more than once – the last value applies (line {line})
speed_client_text: How fast your Wi-Fi or LAN to the server is: the browser downloads test data from the server for a few seconds and sends some back.
speed_internet_text: The server's internet connection, measured by the server itself against Cloudflare (speed.cloudflare.com) – the nearest data centre is shown with the result.
speed_units: Connections are given in Mbit/s, file sizes in MB: 8 bits make a byte, so Mbit/s ÷ 8 = MB/s (100 Mbit/s ≈ 12.5 MB/s, 1 Gbit/s ≈ 125 MB/s).
speed_auto_text: Quadeck measures the server's internet connection itself – for the graph and, if you like, a notification when the internet is slow or down.
speed_auto_data: One measurement downloads at full speed for a few seconds – about 400 MB at 500 Mbit/s. With a data cap, daily is the better choice.
speed_auto_notify: Set up a notification for slow internet
speed_chart_empty: No measurements in this range yet.
speed_alert_slow: Twice too slow recently: {down} Mbit/s instead of at least {expected} Mbit/s.
notify_rule_unitFailedHelp: A systemd unit or a container service is in the state “failed” – e.g. the nightly backup.
notify_rule_serviceDownHelp: The HTTP check of a tile on the overview has been failing for over 2 minutes.
notify_rule_containerUnhealthyHelp: Healthcheck reports “unhealthy” or a container without a unit has crashed (over 2 minutes).
notify_rule_smartHelp: Warning or critical state according to the SMART evaluation.
notify_rule_internetHelp: The automatic measurement of the speed test (Network → Speed test) is too slow twice in a row, or Cloudflare is not reachable. Only measures when "Measure automatically" is on.
notify_alert_internetSlow: Internet slow: {down} Mbit/s instead of at least {expected} Mbit/s
notify_rule_updatesHelp: Once a day: new packages and container images – only if something changed since the last message.
notify_channel_ntfyHelp: Push to your phone via ntfy.sh or your own ntfy server: pick a topic and subscribe to it in the ntfy app.
notify_channel_gotifyHelp: Your own Gotify server: create an app in Gotify and enter its token.
notify_channel_telegramHelp: Create a bot with @BotFather, enter the token, write to the bot and enter the chat ID (e.g. via @userinfobot).
notify_channel_webhookHelp: POST with JSON to a URL – works for Discord, Slack, Mattermost, Home Assistant or your own scripts.
notify_channel_emailHelp: Via the SMTP server of your mail provider. Gmail, GMX, web.de and the like often need a separate app password for this, not the normal password.
notify_provider_gmailNote: App password at myaccount.google.com → Security (2-factor must be on)
notify_error_passwordUnencrypted: Only send a password with encryption (SSL/TLS or STARTTLS)
notify_error_recipients: Recipients: one or more e-mail addresses (comma-separated)
notify_alert_oomKilled: killed by the kernel for lack of memory
notify_error_emailNotHttp: E-mail goes via SMTP, not HTTP
notify_email_footer: Sent by Quadeck. Change notifications: Quadeck → Notifications.
shares_check_rootDir: The root directory cannot be shared
shares_check_nameInvalid: Name: letters, digits, spaces, “_ . - $”, max. 80 characters
shares_check_usersInvalid: Users: names or @group, separated by spaces
shares_check_clientInvalid: Client “{host}”: IP, network (192.168.1.0/24), host name or *
shares_check_rwAndRo: {host}: rw and ro at the same time
smart_status_failurePredicted: The drive itself reports an imminent failure
smart_status_prefailNow: A pre-failure attribute is below its threshold now
smart_status_prefailPast: A pre-failure attribute was below its threshold in the past
smart_status_errorLog: Errors in the drive's error log
smart_label_crcErrors: transfer errors (CRC) – usually cable or backplane
smart_note_crcNew: {added} new transfer errors (CRC) since {since} – {count} in total; check cable or backplane
smart_note_crcOld: {count} older transfer errors (CRC), none new since {since} – the counter is never reset, only an increase would be a problem
smart_note_crcTotal: {count} transfer errors (CRC) since installation – the counter is never reset; Quadeck will tell you as soon as new ones appear
smart_hint_replaceDrive: Get a replacement and back up your data – the drive shows wear or defects.
smart_hint_checkCable: Check or replace the SATA cable and power connector; the drive itself is often fine. The CRC counter then stops but does not go back – if it no longer rises, the problem is fixed.
smart_hint_improveCooling: Improve cooling (airflow, fans, spacing between the drives).
smart_hint_unreadable: smartctl cannot read the drive – USB enclosure without SAT support or missing permissions.
ssh_error_allowUsers: Allowed users: names separated by spaces
timers_check_invalidCommand: Command contains control characters or is too long
timers_check_workDirAbsolute: Working directory must be an absolute path
timers_describe_dayNames: Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri Sat Sun
timers_cron_weekdayStep: systemd does not support steps for weekdays
timers_cron_reboot: @reboot is not a schedule – a unit with WantedBy=multi-user.target fits better
timers_cron_fieldCount: Cron needs five fields: minute hour day month weekday
timers_cron_dayOrWeekday: Cron runs when the day OR the weekday matches – systemd requires both. Please check.
unitFiles_check_overrideAppends: {key}= only adds in an override – to replace, insert an empty {key}= line before it
unitFiles_check_noSection: No [Section] – a unit needs at least [Unit] or [Service]
units_failure_oomLimit: OOM kill: memory limit MemoryMax={limit} reached
units_failure_oomKernel: OOM kill: terminated by the kernel due to low memory
units_failure_timeout: Timed out while starting or stopping
units_failure_startLimit: Too many restarts in a short time (start limit)
units_failure_resources: Resources missing (e.g. image, volume or network)
users_group_systemdJournal: Read the journal of all services
users_error_invalidName: Name: lowercase letters, digits, - and _ (starting with a letter), at most 32 characters
users_error_fullNameInvalid: Full name: no colon, comma or line break
users_error_lastAdmin: Afterwards nobody could log in as administrator anymore – Quadeck could not be unlocked and sudo would no longer work. Give another administrator a password first.
users_describe_setPassword: Sets a new password for {name}. Running sessions stay logged in.
users_describe_lock: Locks {name}: no more logins, not even with an SSH key. Running sessions and services of the account keep running.
users_describe_setSamba: Sets the Samba password of {name} (for network shares, separate from the login password).
quadletHelp_container_Image: Image, preferably fully qualified (docker.io/…), otherwise AutoUpdate=registry does not work.
quadletHelp_container_ContainerName: Name of the container (default: systemd-<file name>).
quadletHelp_container_Volume: Mount a volume or directory: source:target[:options]; .volume files as name.volume.
quadletHelp_container_Network: Network: host, none, a Podman network or a .network file (name.network).
quadletHelp_container_AutoUpdate: registry: podman auto-update pulls new images; local: only locally built ones.
quadletHelp_container_Exec: Arguments for the command in the image (replaces CMD).
quadletHelp_container_User: User in the container (UID or name).
quadletHelp_container_UserNS: User namespace, e.g. keep-id or auto.
quadletHelp_container_HealthOnFailure: Action when unhealthy: none, kill, restart, stop.
quadletHelp_container_Pod: Pod (.pod file) the container runs in.
quadletHelp_container_IP: Static IPv4 address in the network.
quadletHelp_container_IP6: Static IPv6 address in the network.
quadletHelp_container_Timezone: Time zone, e.g. local or Europe/Berlin.
quadletHelp_container_NoNewPrivileges: No new privileges in the container.
quadletHelp_container_Pull: Pull policy: always, missing, never, newer.
quadletHelp_container_Rootfs: Root file system instead of an image.
quadletHelp_container_ServiceName: Override the name of the systemd unit.
quadletHelp_pod_ExitPolicy: Behaviour when all containers have exited.
quadletHelp_network_NetworkName: Name of the Podman network (default: systemd-<file name>).
quadletHelp_volume_VolumeName: Name of the volume (default: systemd-<file name>).
quadletHelp_volume_Copy: Copy the content of the image into the volume.
quadletHelp_image_ImageTag: Name the image is referenced by.
quadletHelp_systemd_Requires: Start these units too; if one fails, this one stops as well.
unitHelp_unit_After: Start only after these units (e.g. network-online.target).
unitHelp_unit_Requires: Start these units too; if one fails, this one stops as well.
unitHelp_unit_ConditionPathExists: Only start if the path exists (e.g. a mounted disk).
unitHelp_service_Type: simple: runs permanently · oneshot: script that exits · notify/forking: as the program requires.
unitHelp_service_ExecStart: Command with full path. In an override, set an empty ExecStart= first.
unitHelp_service_EnvironmentFile: File with variables (leading -: may be missing).
unitHelp_service_TimeoutStartSec: How long the start may take, e.g. 90s or infinity.
unitHelp_service_MemoryMax: Memory limit, e.g. 2G – above it the kernel kills the service.
unitHelp_service_CPUQuota: CPU limit, e.g. 50% (of one core) or 200%.
unitHelp_service_ProtectSystem: Read-only system: full = /usr, /boot, /etc · strict = everything except allowed paths.
unitHelp_service_ProtectHome: Hide home directories or make them read-only.
unitHelp_timer_OnCalendar: Schedule, e.g. *-*-* 03:00:00 or Mon..Fri 07:30. In an override, set an empty OnCalendar= first.
unitHelp_timer_OnUnitActiveSec: Repeat this long after the last start, e.g. 1h.
unitHelp_install_WantedBy: Start at boot: multi-user.target (services) or timers.target (timers).
fstab_option_defaults: Default settings (rw, suid, dev, exec, auto, nouser, async).
fstab_option_nofail: If the disk is missing at boot, the server boots anyway – without this option it ends up in emergency mode.
fstab_option_xsystemddevicetimeout: How long systemd waits for the disk at boot (default 90 s).
fstab_option_noauto: Do not mount at boot, only by hand or on demand.
fstab_option_xsystemdautomount: Mount on first access only – the boot does not wait for the disk.
fstab_option_xsystemdidletimeout: With automount: unmount again after this much idle time (the disk may sleep).
fstab_option_xsystemdmounttimeout: Maximum time for the mount itself.
fstab_option_xsystemdrequires: Mount only once this unit is running.
fstab_option_xsystemdmakefs: Format an empty device at boot – careful.
fstab_option_xmountmkdir: Create the mount point if it is missing.
fstab_option_xgvfsshow: Show in the desktop file manager.
fstab_option_netdev: Needs the network – mount only after it is up.
fstab_option_noatime: Do not write access times – fewer writes, disks sleep longer.
fstab_option_relatime: Update the access time only rarely (default).
fstab_option_lazytime: Keep timestamps in memory only and write them in batches.
fstab_option_users: Any user may mount and unmount.
fstab_option_owner: The owner of the device may mount.
fstab_option_group: The group of the device may mount.
fstab_option_exec: Programs on the disk may run (default).
fstab_option_noexec: Do not run programs from this disk.
fstab_option_nosuid: Setuid bits are ignored – safer for data disks.
fstab_option_nodev: Device files are ignored – safer for data disks.
fstab_option_discard: TRIM on every delete – for SSDs the weekly fstrim.timer is usually better.
fstab_option_errors: On errors: continue, remount-ro or panic.
fstab_option_commit: Write to the disk every this many seconds.
fstab_option_data: Journal mode: ordered, writeback or journal.
fstab_option_nobarrier: Without write barriers – only with a battery-backed cache.
fstab_option_inode64: Create inodes anywhere on the disk (default).
fstab_option_allocsize: Size reserved in advance when writing.
fstab_option_compress: Compress new files, e.g. zstd or zstd:3.
fstab_option_compressforce: Always compress, even poorly compressible files.
fstab_option_spacecache: Free space cache, v2 is the default.
fstab_option_degraded: Mount even with a disk missing from the RAID.
fstab_option_uid: Owner of all files (user ID) – this file system has no Linux permissions.
fstab_option_umask: Permissions that are removed, e.g. 022 (others may only read) or 002.
fstab_option_iocharset: Character set of the file names, e.g. utf8.
fstab_option_flush: Write earlier – safer for removable media.
fstab_option_windowsnames: Do not create names Windows cannot open.
fstab_option_prealloc: Reserve space in advance when writing – less fragmentation.
fstab_option_force: Mount even if Windows marked the disk as “dirty”.
fstab_option_credentials: File with user name and password.
fstab_option_soft: If the server fails, return an error instead of waiting.
fstab_option_x: Option for systemd or other programs (ignored by the kernel).
boot_flavor_linux_text: Latest stable version – the default kernel of Arch.
boot_flavor_linuxlts_text: Long-term kernel, rarely changes – the classic way back when an update of linux causes trouble.
boot_flavor_linuxzen_text: Tuned for short response times – more for desktops and gaming.
boot_flavor_linuxhardened_text: With extra hardening; some programs do not run with it.
users_describe_withoutPassword: , without password – login only with an SSH key

match.admin=true: Saves name, shell and groups of {name} (administrator via {group}). New groups apply from the next login.
match.admin=*: Saves name, shell and groups of {name}. New groups apply from the next login.

match.removeHome=true: Deletes {name} along with the home directory and mail spool – the files will be gone.
match.removeHome=*: Deletes {name}; the home directory is kept.

match.isDefault=true: “{title}” points to missing files ({files}) – the server will not boot with this entry. It is the default entry!
match.isDefault=*: “{title}” points to missing files ({files}) – the server will not boot with this entry (e.g. after removing a kernel – remove the entry)

match.canInstall=true: Only one kernel installed. A second one (e.g. linux-lts) is a way out if a kernel update causes trouble – then “boot linux-lts once”. Install it below under “Kernel”.
match.canInstall=*: Only one kernel installed. A second one (e.g. linux-lts) is a way out if a kernel update causes trouble – then “boot linux-lts once”.

ssh_error_noInclude: {file} does not include sshd_config.d/*.conf – add “Include /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf” at the top

match.password=true: Saved, but sshd uses different values (password login on, root {root}) – another file in sshd_config.d or sshd_config sets them first.
match.password=*: Saved, but sshd uses different values (password login off, root {root}) – another file in sshd_config.d or sshd_config sets them first.

match.hasPackage=true: Driver for {fsType} is missing – install package {package}

backup_empty_text: Quadeck backs up the data of your containers, /etc and the Quadlet files with restic: encrypted, deduplicated, on a schedule. The target can be a second disk, a NAS over SFTP, Backblaze B2, S3 or a REST server.
backup_repoError: The repository was not reachable when last read: {message}
backup_password_warn: Keep the repository password somewhere other than this server. If the server dies, the backups cannot be read without it.
backup_password_text: With this password and the target, the backups open with restic on any computer. Keep it in a password manager or on paper, not only on this server.
backup_disable_text: The schedule is removed and no more backups run. The repository with all snapshots, the password and the credentials stay.
backup_estimate: about {count} snapshots, the oldest about {days} days back
backup_kindHelp_local: a different disk than the data
backup_runs_chart: New data per backup, the last 14
backup_runs_none: No run yet. The first backup starts on schedule or with “Back up now”.
backup_browse_empty: This folder is empty in the backup.
backup_restore_pick: Select files or folders on the left.
backup_restore_inPlaceStop: overwrites today’s files; {units} is stopped meanwhile
backup_restore_job: Runs as a job with progress (restic restore), after unlocking.

backup_setup_localHint: The parent folder must exist (disk mounted), otherwise nothing is created. Use a different disk than the data.
backup_setup_sftpHint: root needs an SSH key without passphrase for the target (ssh-copy-id as root).
backup_setup_passwordNote: Quadeck generates the repository password and stores it readable for root only. Afterwards the page shows it to you to keep it safe.
backup_setup_whatHelp: Suggested from your Quadlets: their folders and volumes, plus /etc. Media mounted read-only are not preselected.
backup_setup_patternsHelp: * any characters · ** any number of folders · without / the pattern applies in every folder
backup_setup_sizesHint: How big will the backup be? Measuring the folders takes a while with many files.
